record_reviews.source_kind: incoming letter, memorandum or quoted extract
record_reviews.summary: Bronn asks whether a new English Origin edition is forthcoming, then lays out his qualified view that Darwin’s theory is the only natural route to resolving creation while current knowledge of abiogenesis remains negative. He thanks Darwin for the Primula paper and says Darwin’s observations have directed his attention. German body with several restored lacunae; Bronn’s closing is preserved.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin gives E. A. Smith detailed instructions for preserving and redrawing engraved plates: grouping crab, butterfly and Landois figures, adjusting reference letters, dotted lines, skin outlines and block placement. The closing gives return addresses and says the plates are to be left until called for. This is a rendering/production memorandum, not scientific argument.

record_reviews.source_kind: incoming letter, memorandum or quoted extract
record_reviews.summary: Mary Butler reports family health news and asks Darwin whether he can help Mr Thom, a 33-year-old man forced toward Queensland after office work damaged his health. She gives his character and testimonials, notes failed job applications, reports Mr Smyth’s Trinidad appointment, and closes with personal news about Darwin’s beard. Social appeal with no scientific prompt.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Cambridge’s question about sexual selection. He distinguishes reproductive organs from sexual selection, discusses male variability, sex differences in colour, display, stridulating organs and spiders, and closes with a qualified Canestrini report and his old Beagle spider collection. His argument is sustained across seven substantive blocks; the supplied date is a boundary probe.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks the Duke of Argyll to read a memorial supporting Wallace and, if he would sign as a scientific worker, inform Gladstone. Darwin acknowledges Argyll’s disagreement with Wallace but says it should not affect judgement of Wallace’s scientific career. The request is political/institutional advocacy, with no reply preserved.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin critiques Grant Allen’s book after a deliberately uncritical first reading: corrections on Sprengel, Wiesner, cryptogamic plants and sexes, a rejection of Allen’s pleasure/pain theory, defence of sexual selection against Wallace, and references to Hochberg and Fritz Müller. He marks excisions and admits his amanuensis is away, while a final block asks whether Allen received an earlier acknowledgement.

record_reviews.source_kind: incoming letter, memorandum or quoted extract
record_reviews.summary: Chance challenges Darwin’s Descent claim that the beard is generally lighter than head hair. He identifies himself as an exception, encloses hair/beard specimens, gives family-colour reasoning, reports looking for other cases, and argues exceptions need not invalidate Darwin’s rule. This is an incoming counterexample with no Darwin answer in the record.
